summary: Eve Bouffard frames 'Imagination Engineering' as the defining challenge of the AI era: with increasingly powerful models, the bottleneck is no longer technical execution but the ability to dream up crazy, bold ideas. She invokes the Library of Alexandria as an analogy for our current moment, urging focus on consolidating and creating knowledge for humanity. Inspired by Paul Graham's practice of 'thinking in public' through essays, and by a colleague's 'Lewis Thoughts' Slack channel, Eve created 'Eve Thoughts' to share her stream of consciousness with trusted YC colleagues. After a week of brain-dumping, she used Opus 4.8 to aggregate these thoughts into a personal interactive website (evebufar.com) that automatically identified her interests in art, books, quotes, and tools, and offered extensive customization including shaders, fonts, multilingual translation, a voice/tone MD profile, and an auto-updating design system. She demonstrates the 'Shape of Minds' tool, built the same morning, which maps commonalities across dimensions like thinking, obsessions, routines, and worldview among historical geniuses such as Bach, Da Vinci, Dali, Marie Curie, Tesla, and Einstein. She also shows a custom emoji picker built to solve her own frustration with finding the right emoji. Throughout, she emphasizes 'software on demand'—any stream of consciousness can be instantly turned into a functional tool by an AI agent. Eve extends this philosophy to learning, requesting short AI-generated reports on topics like the 10 principles of good design and Renaissance patronage, which she digests during commutes. She anticipates using Cloud Workspaces and Conductor Cloud to spin off agents on the go, and shows a repository evolution backlog tracking changes to the Shape of Minds project. She references Gary's characterization of current AI as a 'rocket ship for the mind,' upgrading Steve Jobs' 'bicycle of the mind' metaphor, and PG's prompt: 'live in the future and then build what's missing.' Eve frames all of this as an experiment and invites others to share their own AI experimentation practices.

sections.summary: Eve describes her inspiration from Lewis Thoughts, a colleague's stream-of-consciousness Slack channel, and her creation of Eve Thoughts on the YC Slack to brain-dump everything crossing her mind.

sections.title: Paul Graham and Thinking in Public
sections.summary: Eve discusses Paul Graham's influence, his practice of thinking in public through essays, and how this inspired her experiment of sharing her stream of consciousness with trusted YC colleagues.

sections.title: Website Demo: evebufar.com
sections.summary: Eve demonstrates her AI-generated personal website that aggregates a week of thoughts, automatically identifying interests in art, books, quotes, and tools. The site offers customization including shaders, fonts, multilingual translation, voice/tone profiles, and an auto-updating design system.

sections.title: Shape of Minds Project
sections.summary: Eve showcases an interactive tool built the same morning that maps commonalities across dimensions like thinking, obsessions, routines, and worldview among historical geniuses such as Bach, Da Vinci, Dali, Marie Curie, Tesla, and Einstein.

sections.title: Software on Demand and Emoji Picker
sections.summary: Eve demonstrates a custom Slack emoji picker tool and emphasizes the concept of software on demand—turning any stream of consciousness into a functional application by asking an AI agent.

sections.title: AI for Rapid Learning and Repository Evolution
sections.summary: Eve describes building the emoji picker to solve her own struggle with finding the right emoji, then explains how she uses AI to generate short learning reports on topics like the 10 principles of good design and Renaissance patronage, which she digests during commutes. She anticipates using Cloud Workspaces and Conductor Cloud to spin off agents on the go. She also shows a repository evolution backlog tracking changes to the Shape of Minds project, and closes by framing everything as an experiment and inviting others to share their AI practices.
